brief.headline: Close the 8.6% gap on measuring cups to Premier's ₹0.35/NOS and tighten payment to 30 days to free up ₹10.19 L cash

priceAsk.summary: Match Premier Plastic's ₹0.35/NOS on the measuring-cup SKU and bring the overall spend down by ₹82500 annually
priceAsk.basis: We pay Mars ₹0.38/NOS for MESU. CUP 30MM TRANS.PP 2.5/5/10ML — that's 8.6% more than Premier's ₹0.35/NOS. Open-market asks for similar 28 mm PP caps sit at ₹0.55–1.20/pc (typical ₹0.85–0.95), so Mars has room to drop to our best price and still be market-fair.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days after receipt to 30 days

brief.financialLeverage: Mars Plastics publishes no financials, so we can't see their revenue, profit or how tight cash is for them. Our ₹1.24 Cr annual spend is meaningful but we have no ratio to judge exactly how much. Without their numbers, we build our case on what we do know: Premier beats them by 8.6% on the key SKU, the open market shows headroom, and we have five credible second sources lined up. Push firmly on price and payment, but keep the tone professional — if they push back hard we qualify an alternate and shift volume.

evidence.point: Premier Plastic sells us the same measuring-cup part for less
Closing that gap saves us real money every year
Switching to 30-day payment frees up cash we can use elsewhere
Open-market asking prices for similar PP caps give Mars room to move
evidence.figure: ₹0.55–1.20/pc ask band, typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc — verdict: MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume

evidence.point: Mars supplies us one category and our spend with them is modest
evidence.figure: ₹1.24 Cr annual on Rigid plastic packaging

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score B (65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms. Top second-source candidate and already qualified for packaging.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader, ₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health B (73/100) — pails, containers, pharma packaging. Strong, profitable, robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited (lead to qualify)
alternates.why: Pan-India manufacturer (medium confidence from web research) — verify capability and price before sending RFQ.

risks: Mars publishes no financials, so we're flying blind on their stability — if they're fragile, a hard push might backfire; watch for signs of distress in the room.
Premier already beats Mars on price for the key SKU, so Mars may refuse to match — be ready to shift that SKU's volume to Premier and use the threat to move the rest to Manjushree or Mold-Tek.
We have no multi-year contract or volume commitment with Mars — they may dig in if they think we'll walk anyway; clarify that hitting these terms keeps them in the mix for future tenders.
The market-ask data is for a 28 mm cap, not our exact 30 mm measuring cup — if Mars calls out the spec difference, pivot to the Premier benchmark (same part, same spec, lower price) as the anchor.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to keep Mars in our supply base, but right now Premier is giving us the same measuring cup at ₹0.35 and you're at ₹0.38 — let's talk about how we close that gap and tighten payment terms so this relationship works for both of us.
